topics.topic: Behavior when credential scanning cannot be completed
questions: What happens if the complete body cannot be searched because it exceeds a bound, cannot be buffered, is truncated, or raises a read error?
What happens if the kernel cannot complete the search—for example because reading the body fails or the scan exceeds a resource bound?
What happens if the complete body cannot be searched because reading, decoding, size enforcement, or the search itself fails?

quotes: send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] MUST bound connecting, writing and reading the whole response by one deadline, the monotonic_ns reading taken before connecting plus the imported RELEASE_CEILING_TRANSPORT_TIMEOUT_MS constant in nanoseconds, held in a local variable only and never stored; each socket wait is given the time left rounded up to whole milliseconds, and the deadline has passed once a later monotonic_ns reading reaches it; the response body is counted after transfer decoding and read at most to the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant, a longer body being over the ceiling.

send_prepared_request: [BEHAVIOR] The outcome is decided in this order, with effect_class read meaning the read column: a failure of name resolution, connection or TLS before the first request byte was written is service_unreachable, attempt not_sent for other classes; a timeout, reset, end of stream, malformed status line or headers — a status line and header section longer together than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant included —, or only 1xx after the first byte was written is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 3xx is operation_failed with detail redirect_not_followed for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 5xx is service_unreachable for read and outcome_unknown with attempt unknown otherwise; 4xx is operation_refused, attempt not_applied for other classes; 2xx whose body is longer than the imported RELEASE_CEILING_SERVICE_RESPONSE_BYTES_MAX constant, whatever its output ports, or whose body as read contains the bytes of the credential value sent, searched before parsing, or whose outputs do not fit is contract_violation, attempt applied for other classes; 2xx whose outputs fit is succeeded, attempt applied for other classes.
judgement.why: State 8 notes define bounded post-transfer reading and classify read failures, timeouts, premature ends, oversized bodies and searchable bounded bodies.

topics.topic: Node and run outcome after detecting an echoed credential
questions: When a credential is found, what observable result, node verdict, run status and refusal or failure reason replace the withheld answer?
When a credential is found, what observable result is recorded for the operation node and run—failure, refusal, another status—and which dependent nodes may continue?
What observable node and run result is produced when a credential is found: which failure reason/code is returned, whether the node is failed, and whether its dependants stop?

quotes:
A 2xx body that echoes it is
   therefore not used: the answer is `contract_violation` (rule 5), no output
   is stored or spooled, and for a non-read operation the attempt is `applied`
   (owner, 2026-10-05: a stored output holding the credential would be the
   kernel writing it).

A failed node stops only its dependants (`upstream_failed`); independent
branches finish (K-09).
judgement.why: The later rules make the node a contract violation with the fixed withholding detail, store no output, mark a non-read attempt applied, and stop only dependent nodes.

topics.topic: Protected credential values and rotation snapshots included in the search set
questions: Which protected values are search needles: only the credential used for the responding service request, every service credential, owner and agent tokens, or every secret in protected configuration, and which configuration snapshot applies during rotation?
Which protected values are search needles: the called service's credential only, every service credential, owner and agent tokens too, and only current values or also rotated values?
What exact credential set is searched: the credential used for that service call, all service credentials, owner and agent tokens, or every secret in protected configuration?

quotes:
Every body as read, whatever its status — reading stops at the ceiling
   (rule 5) — is searched, before it is parsed or cut, for the bytes of the credential
   value sent with the request; when they occur, the body is
   dropped whole and `failure_detail` is exactly `error body withheld: it
   contained the credential` (A17 rule 2).

resolve_service_credential: [BEHAVIOR] MUST find the service_credentials entry of service_id and read, at this call and never earlier, the file at its secret_file path, opened component by component without following a symbolic link at any component, the checks and the read using that one opened file, which must be a regular file, owned by the process's effective user and granting no permission to group or others; the value is the file's content decoded as UTF-8 with exactly one trailing newline removed when present.
resolve_service_credential: [RETURN_SHAPE] Returns ResolvedCredential with the configured header_name and the resolved header_value, for the one request being built.
judgement.why: Only the called service's credential value resolved for and sent with that request is searched, so unrelated tokens and credentials are excluded and rotation is sampled when the request is built.

topics.topic: Representation and comparison rules for verbatim credential matching
questions: What exact representation and comparison define a verbatim credential match inside textual and binary files?
What exact byte-level rule defines a verbatim match in textual and binary bodies, including character encoding, substring matches, and credentials that are not represented as text?
Against which representation is verbatim matching performed, including transfer/content decoding, character encoding, Unicode normalization, multipart framing, and matches spanning streamed chunks?

quotes:
The kernel asks for no content encoding (`Accept-Encoding: identity`); the
   size counted is the response body's bytes after transfer decoding.

Every body as read, whatever its status — reading stops at the ceiling
   (rule 5) — is searched, before it is parsed or cut, for the bytes of the credential
   value sent with the request; when they occur, the body is
   dropped whole and `failure_detail` is exactly `error body withheld: it
   contained the credential` (A17 rule 2).

Only that verbatim echo is
   searched for; a body carrying the credential in another encoding is kept
   like any other and is protected only by its class.
judgement.why: The later service rule specifies an exact byte-subsequence search over the transfer-decoded body before parsing or cutting, with identity content encoding and no recognition of alternate encodings.

topics.topic: Retention or deletion of credential-bearing bodies and derived records
questions: After detecting a credential, may the body or file remain in the run spool, failed-run retention, digests, traces or trial fixtures, or must every copy and derived record be discarded?
After a match, may the kernel retain the response body or file in the run spool, trace-related storage, or trial evidence, or must it delete it immediately while retaining only non-secret metadata?

After detection, is the credential-bearing body immediately discarded, retained in the run spool, retained in a quarantine record, or represented only by metadata or a digest; and what happens for a failed run whose spool would normally be retained?

quotes:
when they occur, the body is
   dropped whole and `failure_detail` is exactly `error body withheld: it
   contained the credential` (A17 rule 2). A 2xx body that echoes it is
   therefore not used: the answer is `contract_violation` (rule 5), no output
   is stored or spooled, and for a non-read operation the attempt is `applied`
   (owner, 2026-10-05: a stored output holding the credential would be the
   kernel writing it).

A 401 whose body echoes the credential value keeps `failure_detail` exactly
   `error body withheld: it contained the credential`, and the credential
   appears in no record.

A 2xx JSON body that echoes the credential value in a member an output port
   takes concludes `contract_violation` with that same `failure_detail`, and
   no StoredValue holds the credential.
judgement.why: The body is dropped whole, never stored or spooled as output, and the credential appears in no record or StoredValue, leaving only the fixed non-secret failure detail.

topics.topic: Bodies and outputs covered by credential scanning
questions: Which bodies must the kernel search: only microservice operation response bodies, or also function results, MCP responses, and other bodies it handles?
Which bodies are searched: only HTTP response bodies returned by microservice operations, kernel MCP answers too, sandbox outputs, multipart parts, and/or files subsequently moving through the spool?

quotes:
A09: building one HTTP request from a binding, the selected instance and the
node's inputs — URL, query and body encoding, headers, the credential — and
sending it once with no redirect, proxy or retry; the outcome table of A09 rule
5; the pre-send checks of the instance and the inputs (A09 rule 6). Withholding
any body that echoes the credential before it becomes an output or `failure_detail`
(A09 rule 7), since only it holds the credential at the answer.

Every body as read, whatever its status — reading stops at the ceiling
   (rule 5) — is searched, before it is parsed or cut, for the bytes of the credential
   value sent with the request; when they occur, the body is
   dropped whole and `failure_detail` is exactly `error body withheld: it
   contained the credential` (A17 rule 2).
judgement.why: The later module boundary assigns scanning specifically to the service invoker for HTTP response bodies carrying the credential it sent, not to sandbox results, MCP answers, or files already in the spool.

topics.topic: Effect status and retry policy when an effect response contains a credential
questions: When an effect request was sent and its response body contains a credential, is the effect recorded as applied, unknown, or failed, and may it ever be resent?

topics.topic: Whether credential-echo scanning is an automatic kernel action and how its actor is recorded
questions: Is credential-echo detection another automatic kernel action, and must records identify the kernel as its actor?
